issues.passage: Funding decisions were made irrespective of need, meaning only the wealthiest applicants were considered.
issues.why: Irrespective of need correctly means without regard to need; the sentence uses the word properly (need was ignored).

fix.correctPassage: The scholarship is awarded on academic merit, irrespective of family income.
wrongPassages: Funding decisions were made irrespective of need, carefully ranking every applicant by how urgently help was required.
The policy applies irrespective of major only when the major is engineering.
She chose the laboratory assignment irrespective of her interest, carefully matching every preference.
